standard.title: Interpret and translate for intercultural understanding
standard.description: interpret and translate non-verbal, spoken and written interactions and texts to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can interpret and adjust language for cultural contexts — including context-dependent meaning, translation comparison and cultural response creation (AC9LS8C04). They have not yet worked systematically with creative text translation, evaluated translation tools critically, or reflected on intercultural miscommunication.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret and translate target language interactions and texts to convey meaning and intercultural understanding — including creative text translation, tool evaluation, and reflection on intercultural miscommunication.

nodes.label: Translating and comparing translations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can translate short target language texts and compare their translation with others' — analysing similarities, differences and possible explanations.
nodes.minimum_width: Translate a short familiar text and compare with at least one other translation — identify at least two translation decisions and explain each.
nodes.typical_width: Translate short target language texts across varied text types; compare translations with classmates; analyse similarities and differences between versions; consider possible reasons for translation variation; reflect on challenges of achieving equivalence.
wider: Translate a creative text (song, poem, advertisement) and annotate every decision point — explain where literal translation was abandoned and why
Compare three different translations of the same text — identify what each prioritises (literal accuracy, cultural resonance, readability) and evaluate the trade-offs
nodes.hinge_reason: Translation comparison — reflecting on why versions differ — is the analytical foundation for all deeper translation work. Students who translate without comparing cannot develop the metacognitive awareness of translation as decision-making.

response_modes.reason: Translation decision analysis requires students to articulate the reasons behind choices — not only make them. Comparative annotation tasks scaffold this explicit reasoning.

success_criteria: Translates a short text and compares with at least one other translation
Identifies at least two translation decisions and explains the reasoning for each

nodes.label: Evaluating translation tools and creative translation challenges
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the accuracy, efficiency and reliability of translation tools, and reflect on the specific challenges of translating creative and culturally specific content.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate at least one translation tool for a specific text — identify at least two limitations; identify at least one creative or culturally specific expression where equivalence is not achievable.
nodes.typical_width: Use, compare and evaluate online translation tools for accuracy and reliability; discuss risks of over-reliance on automated translation; experiment with translating idiomatic and culturally specific expressions; reflect on the difficulty of achieving equivalence in creative texts.
wider: Evaluate an automated translation of a target language text — identify every error, ambiguity or cultural loss and explain what each reveals about the limits of machine translation
Translate a culturally specific text and produce a translator's note — explaining the most challenging decisions and the strategies used

response_modes.reason: Critical evaluation of translation tools requires explicit evaluation criteria — students need to be able to articulate what makes a translation accurate, appropriate and culturally sensitive.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Critical evaluation of automated translation tools is a genuinely contemporary skill — students who understand the limits of machine translation are better equipped for real-world target language use.
success_criteria: Evaluates at least one translation tool and identifies at least two specific limitations
Identifies at least one expression where equivalence is not achievable and explains why

nodes.label: Creating bilingual texts and reflecting on intercultural miscommunication
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create bilingual texts for target language community audiences and reflect on how meaning can be misinterpreted in intercultural interactions.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a bilingual text for a target language community audience — making at least two deliberate decisions about cultural explanation vs translation; reflect on at least one instance of potential intercultural miscommunication.
nodes.typical_width: Create bilingual texts presenting aspects of Australian culture for target language community audiences; consider how to maintain integrity of original texts when translating culture-specific content; reflect on experiences of miscommunication and strategies for managing it; discuss how meaning can shift in intercultural interactions.
wider: Create a bilingual text for a real target language community audience — include a reflective note on the most challenging decisions about cultural explanation vs translation
Research and present instances where target language-English intercultural communication has produced misunderstanding — explain the mechanisms that caused each

response_modes.reason: Creating bilingual texts for genuine audiences integrates translation skill (N1), tool awareness (N2), and intercultural reflection — all applied in a purposeful mediating act for a real recipient.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Creating bilingual cultural texts for real target language community audiences is the fullest expression of intercultural mediation in this sequence — students are genuine cultural brokers.
success_criteria: Creates a bilingual text with at least two deliberate decisions about cultural explanation vs translation explained
Reflects on at least one instance of potential intercultural miscommunication and proposes a strategy for managing it
